subject: Computer Networking
title: Satellite Internet Constellations
description: A micro-lesson that makes Satellite Internet Constellations usable.

hook.text: Thousands of satellites orbit Earth right now, beaming internet to places no cable will ever reach.

buildup.text: Starlink, Kuiper, and OneWeb deploy Low Earth Orbit satellites at 550 km altitude for low-latency broadband.

discovery.text: LEO satellites orbit fast — your connection hands off between satellites as they pass overhead in minutes.

twist.text: Thousands of satellites create debris risks. Crowded orbits could trigger cascading collisions — Kessler syndrome.

climax.text: Satellite internet serves ships, planes, rural farms, and disaster zones. It complements fiber, not replaces it.

punchline.text: Satellite internet fills the gaps that cables can't reach.

quiz.question: Why do LEO satellites provide lower latency than geostationary ones?
options: They orbit much closer to Earth — 550 km vs 36,000 km

details.summary: Satellite internet constellations like Starlink deploy thousands of low-Earth orbit satellites to provide broadband coverage globally, including rural and remote areas. LEO orbits at 550 km deliver latency below 50 ms, far lower than traditional geostationary satellites at 36,000 km.
details.whyItMatters: Satellite constellations are bridging the digital divide, bringing broadband to areas where terrestrial infrastructure is impractical. They represent the most significant expansion of internet access since undersea cables.
takeaways: LEO satellites orbit at 550 km for low-latency broadband
Thousands of satellites provide continuous global coverage
Rural and remote areas gain broadband access for the first time

faq.question: How does Starlink achieve low latency?
faq.answer: Traditional geostationary satellites orbit at 36,000 km causing 600 ms round-trip latency. Starlink satellites orbit at 550 km, reducing round-trip latency to 20 to 40 ms — comparable to terrestrial broadband. Thousands of satellites ensure at least one is always overhead at any location.

faq.question: What are the limitations of satellite internet?
faq.answer: Weather, trees, and buildings can obstruct satellite signals. Bandwidth is shared among users in an area, causing congestion in dense regions. Equipment costs remain higher than terrestrial alternatives. Space debris concerns grow with thousands of satellites.
